resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR entry gives a 45-foot height. Metro Parks says 82 feet from the ground to the floor of the cab and calls the whole structure a 100-foot tower in its release. The story uses Metro Parks' 82 feet to the cab floor (about 25 m) and reports the 45-foot figure as the register's; the 100-foot figure is not explained.

Metro Parks says the tower was set up in Jackson County in 1942 and also that it was erected 82 years before its 2023 move, which points to 1941. The story gives both and says the year is uncertain. The event is recorded as 1942 with the note.

The Metro Parks media release (August 10, 2023) calls the donor an anonymous private landowner. The later Metro Parks blog names Justin Taylor, on behalf of the entire Taylor family. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Height, build year and donor conflict across sources; see resolved_conflicts. The NHLR visit report (April 2019) predates the 2023 move and is used only for condition, staffing and access before the move. The Metro Parks blog and media release are the main current sources. Current climbing rules beyond daylight hours were not checked, and the park's own web page was not read. No photos added: the NHLR photos are credited but no image URLs were captured. Check 2026-10-09: all 22 quotes were found on the first run; two footnoted claims were corrected (Aermotor 'offered' three designs changed to 'developed' three types, and the donor's family wording now matches the blog's 'entire Taylor family'). The cost, climbing and Grove City claims were already supported and are now backed by added evidence entries.
